distinguishing_features: Adds a physical passive structural element (tuned mass damper with Inconel ring and silicon-nitride shear springs) mounted on the nozzle flange, rather than only software/logic or monitoring.

Shifts the nozzle's dynamic natural frequency and adds structural damping to suppress resonant amplification of thermal transients, rather than capping operating duty or inferring damage thermodynamically.
Acts on the structural dynamic response (mode decoupling / energy absorption) instead of on the thermal load, material strength, or inspection schedule.
Predicts a mechanical stress-amplitude reduction via TMD tuning ratio and effective damping, verifiable by strain or pressure/flow correlation.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Reduce the resonant amplification of small thermal/flow transients into high cyclic stress at the nozzle-to-shell junction without changing static pressure rating or material grade.
parsed.viable_reason: A tuned mass damper is a physically sound, well-established passive vibration absorber, and integrating it into a nozzle flange at moderate mass ratio (mu=0.05, <400C, Inconel 718 / silicon nitride) is feasible and testable, though the 35% RMS claim is optimistic and broadband thermal pulses are not narrowband, so effectiveness is conditional.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: None of the prior art uses a physical passive structural dynamic absorber to detune a nozzle mode; applying a TMD specifically to decouple a pressure-vessel nozzle mode from thermal/flow excitation is a non-routine departure from the monitoring/derating approaches of the closest art.
